USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the G20 dinner with Xi to open a time-limited negotiating track without new unilateral commitments. Keep the existing Section 301 tariffs in place and do not pre-commit to cancelling the scheduled January 1 List 3 step-up or to a purchase-only deal; make any pause of the 10-to-25 percent hike contingent on a written work program with dates and enforcement, not another May-style handshake. Do not launch the threatened additional ~$267 billion list before talks are tested.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is modestly above neutral, not high. Combined US Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B after List 3 took effect at 10% on 2018-09-24, with a legal step-up to 25% set for 2019-01-01 and a further ~$267B list still unused, so Washington still holds unused tariff leverage (timeline 2018-09-17/24; USTR/Federal Register). The core US real economy is not in a tariff recession: industrial production is ~104.1, Michigan sentiment is still 97.5, and CPI is contained. What is biting US interests is concentrated and political: China’s matching retaliation on soy/autos/aircraft has collapsed soybean sales to China by ~94% (China normally takes ~60% of US soy, ~$12B), with harvests rotting or being plowed under and only a fraction of the $12B farm-aid package paid by mid-November. Markets are also signaling cost: VIX is ~18.5 (up ~45% in the window), Baa yields have risen to 5.28%, WTI has fallen to ~$50, and the dollar is stronger. That is farm-belt and financial-volatility pain, not existential supply-chain or ally-cohesion failure — hence +0.12, not +0.5.

Action should be negotiate, not escalate or concede. Escalating into the G20 (or locking in the January hike before Xi is tested) would likely draw further farm/consumer retaliation and a full-coverage tariff war just as APEC already failed to produce a communiqué and China’s Q3 growth has slowed to 6.5% with the yuan ~9% weaker — i.e., Beijing is under pressure and may bargain, but a purchase-only truce already collapsed on 2018-05-29 after the 2018-05-19 joint statement. China’s 142-point list is judged by US officials as lacking timetable and enforcement. Therefore hold the current tariff stock, refuse unilateral rollback or purchase concessions, and use Buenos Aires to explore a delay of the January step-up only against verifiable structural talks.
key_factors: G20 Trump-Xi meeting is the immediate decision node (phone call 2018-11-01; dinner 2018-11-30/12-01)
List 3 already live at 10% on ~$200B; 25% step-up is scheduled for 2019-01-01; unused ~$267B threat remains
US soy channel is badly hit (~94% drop; storage/rot; incomplete farm aid) — concentrated political cost
US macro still resilient (IP, sentiment, CPI); stress is in VIX, credit spreads, oil, and a stronger dollar
China is slowing (Q3 GDP 6.5%, yuan ~-9%) but has not offered enforceable structural change (142-point list)
May 19 purchase truce collapsed within 10 days — do not repeat a handshake-for-purchases deal

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
Trump directs USTR to finalize List 3: 10% tariffs on ~$200B of Chinese imports effective Sept 24, scheduled to rise to 25% on Jan 1, 2019.
Trump and Xi hold a phone call focused on trade; agree to meet at the G20 in Argentina.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory.
US industrial production latest 104.0681 (2018-11-01); still slightly up over the window, not a production collapse.
Michigan consumer sentiment 97.5 in November — high and only marginally softer.
VIX 18.49 on 2018-11-28, +45% over the window after the October spike.
Moody’s Baa corporate yield 5.28 on 2018-11-28, up ~46bp — credit conditions tightening.
Broad dollar index 116.83 on 2018-11-28, +4.5% — tighter financial conditions and pressure on CNY.
American soybean sales to China down 94% from last year’s harvest after China’s retaliatory soybean tariff; China is the largest market for one of America’s largest exports.

Officials say a G20 truce could delay the Jan 1 hike to 25% and hold off ~$267B of new tariffs while talks continue; Kudlow sees a “good possibility” of a deal, but China’s 142-point list is judged to lack timetable and enforcement.
Asked if he would delay or suspend the 10-to-25 percent hike on January 1, Trump said “I think it would be highly unlikely,” signaling he is not expecting a near-term giveaway of leverage.
China growing at slowest pace since the financial crisis; yuan sunk more than 9% vs USD since January; exports still growing but a January step-up to 25% would add pressure.
